title: Immutable input scope of one composite Lara map

x-identity.map_revision_id: sha256("ara.lara-map-revision/v1\0" || JCS(map revision without map_revision_id)); the record holds inputs only, so no exit status, verdict or status can change it

x-consumer-invariants: members are in .laramap member order, which fixes Lara's node numbering, and aliases are unique; each member binds its alias to a full contribution_id, the argument record and bytes, the binding_id and the member's source identity; aliases and Lara's author-declared artifact digests never authenticate a publisher

manifest.digest is the SHA-256 of the exact .laramap bytes; Lara map v1 reads current local paths and does not verify member digests, so the runner materializes the member bytes named here before checking

every member binding names this policy's policy_digest and this registry; a member checked under another policy or registry is excluded (incompatible_policy or vocabulary_mismatch) or rechecked under this one, never silently reused

population.contributions is sorted and is the intended population at visibility sequence population.sequence; every intended contribution is either a member or listed in exclusions (sorted by contribution_id) with a reason, never both, and excluded contributions stay visible and never count toward coverage

coverage scope 'audited' admits only members whose every selected claim has a current authorized approval with matching inputs and no unresolved dispute; 'exploratory' may include other members, is labeled exploratory everywhere, and cannot supply an audited-community verdict

adding or removing a member, changing any argument, binding, policy, registry, checker or the intended population creates a new map_revision_id; earlier revisions and their verdicts, including contests, remain under their own scope
display_name may group revisions for people but never identifies a verdict's scope; no map claims whole-community coverage because all included members passed

map revisions and their checks are published through the same request idempotency, publication and recovery rules as attachments under their own hash domains; listing them in a visibility snapshot needs a later ara.visibility revision
